newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - AUG 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - AUG 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

-- A total of 485,699 small businesses and professionals were fined between 100,000 and 300,000 drachmas for breach of regulations on invoicing in fiscal 1993 following cross-checks by the finance ministry's services. Deputy finance minister George Drys announced that a 'black list' of some 500,000 issuers and receivers of forged invoices has been compiled and made available to the public for their reference.
-- Police has arrested three persons on alleged cracking of the database of stockbroker 'Northern Greece Securities' which resulted in the transfer of small quantities of shares to their accounts.
-- The dollar climbed to a further record fixing rate of 291.43 against the drachma and moved to levels unseen for a number of years against major currencies.

-- Fiscal revenues in July grew 16.0 percent year-on-year against a 1997 target of 15.6 percent, deputy finance minister George Drys told reporters on Monday. Fiscal revenue growth over the first seven months of 1997 is three percentage points lower than the full-year target.

-- The government will place emphasis on industry and development in 1998. The national economy ministry is currently preparing a new law to foster development and the prime minister's advisor Proff Yiannis Spraos is drafting a new report on industry and competitiveness.

-- The development ministry will press ahead with privatisations of ailing industries which are subsided by the state. NIBID bank will select the corporate finance houses which will act as company advisors to those privatisations.

-- CPI inflation, to be officially announced on Wednesday by the National Statistics service, will show marginal improvement in July from June's 5.5 percent rate. But it will ease to 5.0 percent in September before bouncing higher in October.
-- Half-year profits posted by closed-end funds more than doubled year-on-year.
